_comment: One entry per speaker in voice/lines.json. 'design' is the ElevenLabs Voice Design prompt. Speakers with 'remix_of' are remixes of another speaker's voice (same person, different accent): design the base speaker first. voice_id is filled in by 'voices.py pick' or 'voices.py use'.

man.design: An older man in his late sixties from Carbonear, a fishing town on Conception Bay, Newfoundland, in 1964. Thick rural Newfoundland English accent with Irish and West Country English roots: dropped h's, 'by' at the end of sentences. Warm, gravelly, weathered voice, unhurried, friendly and teasing, quick to a hearty laugh.
man.design_sample: 'Ow's she gon', by? Some hot today, wha? I likes me rain, drizzle and fog, I does. Ya won't find any dialects 'ere!

harold.design: A young man in his mid-twenties, a bookish graduate student from a small Newfoundland outport in 1964. Mild Newfoundland accent, softened by university. Curious, polite, earnest and a little nerdy, clear articulate delivery, light warm tone.
harold.design_sample: Well, I'm a graduate student at MUN conducting field work. I'm actually researching Newfoundland dialects! What do you call that one?

harold_local.design: Keep the exact same young man, but change his accent to a broad rural Conception Bay Newfoundland accent he is putting on to fit in: dropped h's, 'b'y', a slightly overdone imitation of outport speech.
harold_local.design_sample: Not too bad, b'y. Some hot, wha? 'Ow's she gon' wit' you? I'm only up the road, b'y, just come in on me bike to see what's on the go.

harold_townie.design: Keep the exact same young man, but change his accent to a careful, standard St. John's city accent, close to standard Canadian English, formal and a little stiff.
harold_townie.design_sample: I'm doing quite well, thank you. And how are you? I'm a graduate student at the university in St. John's, conducting a survey this summer.
